rationale: Greek loanword ἧπαρ with Lyc. ⲍ-onset and possessive prefix. Standard anatomical term; here in the macrocosmic body-schema mapping the liver to the cattle/quadrupeds.
Lyc. with ⲝ for ϫ = ϫⲁⲧϥⲉ 'creeping thing, reptile.' Standard creature-class term for the third stratum of creation (after birds and fish).
Lyc. ⲱⲁⲁⲣ likely = ϣⲁⲁⲣ 'skin, hide.' The outer skin = wall surrounding the cosmos in this macrocosmic body-schema.
Possibly related to ⲥⲓϣⲉ 'bitterness' = bile, the bitter humor. Body-part correspondence with darkness in the schema. Confidence low.
Lyc. ⲙⲉⲍⲧⲉ = ⲙⲟⲥⲧⲉ 'hatred' with possessive prefix. Affective faculty mapped onto cosmic schema.
Lyc. ⲟⲩⲣⲏⲧⲉ = ⲟⲩⲉⲣⲏⲧⲉ 'feet,' plural with possessive prefix. Body-part in the macrocosmic schema.
Lyc. ⲱⲛⲍ̄ = ⲱⲛϩ 'life' with possessive prefix. Standard term identifying the five gods as the cosmic body's living principle.
Privative ⲁⲧ- + ⲛⲕⲟⲧⲕ̄ 'sleep.' 'Those who do not sleep' = the unsleeping cosmic Watchers, a standard Manichaean motif of vigilant cosmic guardians.
Greek κάτοχος 'holder, restrainer' with Lyc. relative ⲫⲉⲧ-. Cosmic Holder figure identified with the first intellectual faculty (Mind). Retained as Greek to preserve technical specificity.
Greek στερέωμα 'firmament, vault of heaven.' Plural here in 'the seventh of the firmaments' — the cosmological seven heavens of Manichaean cosmology.
Greek παλάμη/παλαμᾶσθαι 'contrive, craft.' Here a positive cosmic light-figure (contrasting with the dark Palamas in earlier kephalaia) identified with Teaching.
Lyc. ⲱⲁⲙⲧⲉ = ϣⲟⲙⲧⲉ 'third' (fem. ordinal); ⲍⲓⲕⲱⲛ = εἰκών 'icon, image.' Possibly references the Third Ambassador's image-figure.
ⲧⲁ- ('that of') + ⲡⲧⲏⲩ ('the wind'). Element-correspondence in the cosmic mapping (wind being one of the five light-elements).
